subject: Scoped reliability roadmap and next probes for inference endpoints
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@clearpath.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scoped reliability roadmap and next probes for inference endpoints

Samir — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side based on the call: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary SLOs of interest: 99.95% uptime, p99 latency target of ~120ms for 512-token requests, and a 0.5% monthly error-budget threshold.
- Key failure modes to validate: regional failover behavior, throttling/rate-limit impact under bursty traffic, and leader node preemption during heavy KV-cache use.
- Competitive context: you want apples-to-apples comparisons against HyperscalerX managed endpoints and one self-hosted inference API your infra team runs (CloudServe).

Redwood differentiators to emphasise in tests
- Deterministic fallback routing (policy-based) — preserves low-latency paths while failing open to a lower-cost model variant.
- Prefix/KV caching that reduces p50/p95 token cost without increasing p99 latency under sustained load.
- Transparent error budget breakdown by model variant + request class in our Console.

Proposed scoped probe plan (small, medium, full) — please confirm which you want to prioritize
1) Small (2 days): smoke of failover + basic rate-limit burst (1–2 tenants, 5k requests) — validation of correct fallthrough and no request loss.
2) Medium (4 days): sustained burst tests (25k–50k requests), throttling profiles, and p99 retention; run against Redwood hosted and HyperscalerX managed endpoints.
3) Full (7–10 days): multi-region failover with simulated AZ outage, KV-cache heavy sequences, and blackbox client-side error-rate analysis; include CloudServe if you want self-hosted baseline.

Owners / immediate asks
- Can you confirm whether HyperscalerX and CloudServe should both be included in the Medium test? (Samir)
- If yes, send the HyperscalerX contact + CloudServe endpoint access (Alicia?) — we’ll need API keys and a short test account.
- We attached a starter SLO matrix (slo-matrix.xlsx) with the exact metrics we’ll track; Ben and Hannah will own test orchestration and reporting.

Next steps
- Samir: confirm scope (Small/Medium/Full) and which external providers to include by EOD Tue 6/29.
- Redwood (Ben/Hannah): stand up the test harness and share the Drive folder with logs and dashboards within 48 hours of scope confirmation.

Attachments (1): slo-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your priorities.

--
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0191
Redwood Inference, San Francisco

From: Samir Desai <samir@clearpath.health>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@clearpath.health>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Scoped reliability roadmap and next probes for inference endpoints

Avery — really useful summary, thanks. A few clarifications below.

1) Include both HyperscalerX and CloudServe in the Medium run. HyperscalerX is the default managed baseline our ops team wants; CloudServe is the on-prem instance we run for latency-sensitive customers.
2) For the medium test, add a specific sub-probe for rate limit posture: sustained 10k RPS for 10 minutes, then spike to 25k RPS for 60s to see throttling behavior and tail latency impact.
3) Error budget: we track at both service and customer-level. Please report error budget burn separately for the \"public\" endpoints vs. the \"vpc/private\" paths.

I can provide the CloudServe endpoint and test keys — Alicia will share credentials. Also assigning internal owners: I will own scheduling and provide the production traffic shape to replay.

On the HyperscalerX side, I don’t expect them to give us privileged test harness access; can Redwood run the client-side replay against their public endpoints?

Thanks — Samir

Thanks Samir — we’re aligned on scope. A few logistic points and owners from Redwood: 

- Test orchestration owner: Ben Carter (ben.carter@redwood.com) — responsible for harness, scheduling, and aggregated report.
- Test execution and metrics capture: Hannah Schmitt (hannah.schmitt@redwood.com) — will run the load harness and collect p50/p95/p99, success-rate, and error-budget burn.
- Ingestion of CloudServe endpoints: Hannah will need API keys and a short README on auth (Alicia, can you drop those into the Drive folder?).

Planned timeline (subject to your signoff):
- Tue 6/29: Confirm scope + upload creds.
- Wed 6/30: Small smoke run to validate harness and metric collection (2–3 hours).
- Thu–Fri 7/1–7/2: Medium runs against Redwood hosted + HyperscalerX + CloudServe (staggered windows to avoid cross-contamination).
- Mon 7/5: Draft report with metric comparisons and suggested mitigations.

We’ll instrument the tests to capture the following failover behaviors explicitly:
- Regional AZ failover (simulate dropped region & observe routing/fallback time)
- Throttle behavior when client receives 429 vs when provider enforces queuing
- p99 regression when KV-cache warms and when cache is cold (two phases)

Attached: test-owner-assignments.pdf (PDF listing owners and contact windows). We’ll also populate the Drive folder with the harness and a lightweight script you can run locally to reproduce tests.

Related links I’ll push to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aB2cDexampleDriveLink

— Ben
